sources.title: Netflix 2025 Form 10-K
sources.excerpt: For fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Common stock NFLX NASDAQ Global Select Market. December 31, 2025 outstanding shares 4,222,162,150. Consolidated statements in thousands USD except per-share data: FY2025 revenues 45,183,036; operating income 13,326,603; net income 10,981,201; diluted EPS 2.53; diluted weighted-average shares 4,343,863 thousand. Cash flows FY2025: additions to content assets (17,096,617); change in content liabilities (610,838); content amortization 16,422,166; property/equipment/intangibles depreciation/amortization 333,389; stock-based compensation 368,449; operating cash flow 10,149,273; purchases of property and equipment (688,220); acquisitions (17,194); stock repurchases (9,127,167); equity-award settlement taxes (46,165); stock issuance proceeds 666,965. December 31, 2025 cash/equivalents 9,033,681; short-term investments 28,678; short-term and long-term debt 14,462,836; short-term debt 998,865 and long-term debt 13,463,971; operating lease liabilities 2,513,001. One operating segment; primarily monthly streaming membership fees. Regional FY2025 revenues in thousands: UCAN 19,957,152; EMEA 14,514,646; LATAM 5,357,521; APAC 5,353,717. FY2025/2024/2023 operating margins 29.5%/26.7%/20.6%. Content payments are operating cash flow; accelerated amortization, over 90% expected within four years after first availability. December 31, 2025 total content obligations approximately $24.0 billion, of which $18.4 billion not reflected on balance sheet. Tax incentives lowered FY2025 content amortization approximately $1,000 million. Non-income-tax assessments in Brazil increased other cost of revenue; management does not expect material recurring impact. All share/per-share amounts retroactively adjusted for November 14, 2025 ten-for-one split. Each common share has one vote.

sources.title: Netflix January 20, 2026 shareholder letter
sources.excerpt: FY2025 revenue $45.2B, growth 16%, operating margin 29.5%; ad revenue grew more than 2.5x to over $1.5B; crossed 325M paid memberships in Q4. H2 2025 view hours 96 billion, +2% year over year; branded-original viewing +9%; licensed non-branded viewing declined following elevated 2023-2024 licensing during WGA strike. 2025 operating cash flow $10.1B and FCF $9.5B. FCF exceeded $9B forecast because expected approximately $700M Brazil tax-dispute deposit shifted into 2026. At that date proposed Warner Bros acquisition: all cash $27.75 per WBD share; buybacks to pause for acquisition. FY2026 initial FCF forecast roughly $11B and content cash spend/amortization around 1.1x. December Nielsen US TV viewing share 9.0%; Netflix below 10% in major markets. Appendix FY2025 operating cash flow 10,149,273 thousand; PPE purchases 688,220 thousand; FCF 9,461,053 thousand.

sources.title: Netflix April 16, 2026 shareholder letter
sources.excerpt: Q1 2026 revenue $12,250M +16.2%; operating income $3,957M; margin 32.3%; diluted EPS $1.23. EPS above forecast driven by operating performance and $2.8B Warner Bros termination fee recognized in interest and other income. Q1 operating cash flow $5.3B and FCF $5.1B included $2.8B cash termination-fee receipt. FY2026 FCF forecast raised to approximately $12.5B from $11B primarily due to after-tax fee impact; annual content cash spend/amortization around 1.1x. Declined to raise Warner Bros offer, resumed buybacks: 13.5M shares for $1.3B. March InterPositive acquisition. Ads plan US price $8.99; over 60% of Q1 signups within ads countries; over 4,000 advertisers, +70% year over year; expected approximately $3B 2026 ads revenue, 2x 2025. Company estimated approximately 5% global TV view share and less than 45% of broadband-household TAM penetration at year-end 2025. Reed Hastings would not seek June Board re-election. World Baseball Classic Japan estimated cumulative 31.4M contacts, not deduplicated unique viewers.

sources.title: Netflix July 16, 2026 shareholder letter
sources.excerpt: Q2 2026 revenue $12,560M +13.4% (+12% FX-neutral); operating income $4,193M; margin 33.4% vs 34.1%; net income $3,401M; diluted EPS $0.80 vs $0.72; fully diluted weighted-average shares 4,261M. FY2026 narrowed revenue guidance $51.0-$51.4B, operating margin 31.5%, projected ads approximately $3B (rough doubling), content amortization growth approximately 10%. H1 2026 view hours more than 97 billion, +2%, versus 1.5% FY2025; non-English content more than one-third of viewing. Live expected just over 5% of content spend but approximately 1% of hours; six of ten largest new-member signup days over five years attributable to live programming. Expanded NFL slate; WWE, MLB events and Women's World Cup in ads pitch. Recent US/Mexico/Spain price changes consistent with prior changes and expectations. Beginning 2027 What We Watched moves from semiannual to annual Q1 publication separate from earnings. Q2 operating cash flow 1,743,812 thousand; PPE purchases 218,644 thousand; FCF 1,525,168 thousand. H1 operating cash flow 7,034,017 thousand; PPE purchases 414,774 thousand; FCF 6,619,243 thousand. Q2 cash/equivalents 9,099,232 thousand; short-term investments 28,678 thousand. FY2026 FCF guidance approximately $12.5B; Q2 taxes higher partly due to Warner Bros fee. Q2 stock buybacks $4.7B, April new authorization $25B, remaining authorization $27.1B. End quarter gross debt $14.4B, cash/equivalents $9.1B; $1B debt maturing later in year expected to refinance. FCF defined as operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment. Some PDF appendix cells have broken extraction; canonical annual exact values taken from readable 10-K.

sources.title: Netflix 2026 proxy statement
sources.excerpt: April 16, 2026 proxy for June 4 annual meeting. Reed Hastings not standing for re-election. Jay Hoag did not receive majority election support in 2025 due to less than 75% attendance in 2024; Board rejected offered resignation June 22, 2025; 2025 attendance all eligible Board and nominating meetings. 2025 bonus metrics FX-neutral revenue (35%) and FX-neutral operating margin (65%); equal PSU/RSU long-term equity mix, PSUs relative TSR against S&P500 over single three-year period, RSUs vest quarterly three years. Stock ownership guideline 6x base salary co-CEOs, 3x other executives within five years. Sarandos' son film editor compensation exceeded $120,000 reporting threshold in FY2025; wife producer on two productions eligible up to $500,000 and $800,000 subject to milestones; company says pay consistent with comparable work/industry; audit-committee related-party review policy. All per-share/equity references split-adjusted.

sources.title: Netflix Overview of Content Accounting May 2025
sources.excerpt: ASC920 licensed content and ASC926 produced owned-IP content. Netflix Originals branding does not imply ownership: Wednesday MGM, Emily in Paris Paramount are licensed. Content amortized accelerated on viewing patterns reviewed quarterly, shorter of availability/useful life/10 years; over90% expected within four years. First-run topical sports, talk and live expensed upon airing. Cash-flow additions to content are gross additions not cash paid; additions plus change in content liabilities equals cash spending. Content cash payments front-loaded before launch for produced originals. FCF uses OCF less PPE cash spend; content cash already in OCF. Produced ownership may lower middleman cost and improve global rights/merchandising flexibility. Impairment mainly aggregate monetization-group test, abandoned titles separately. Net content library cannot be used to calculate average amortization life.
